lead: A watermark: a translucent layer of repeated text or images over the content that doesn't block the mouse. The pattern is drawn on a canvas and redrawn when the mode or theme style changes; the layer restores itself when it is removed or its attributes are changed (`antiTamper`).

panel.p1: The watermark lies over this content without blocking clicks or text selection. Switch between light and dark, or change the theme style, and its colour follows.
panel.p2: The watermark layer is a repeated, rotated pattern drawn on a canvas and used as a background.

styling.title: Styling Reference
styling.description: Theme styles handle it in `watermark.css`; it only does positioning and the background, not the look, so it is the same in every theme style.
styling.root: The outer container (`position: relative`), holding the content and the watermark layer
styling.layer: A layer over the content that lets the mouse through, with the canvas-drawn pattern as its background; the pattern, size, offset and stacking are written to its `--wm-image` / `--wm-w` / `--wm-h` / `--wm-ox` / `--wm-oy` / `--wm-z`
